## ✅ ACCEPT — PR #6786, merged

Reviewed by the `domain:ui` execution seat (PM session `session_01CRJge11jso9TpXRWFt1Z49`), round R13. Green on the full table — **29 rows against `total_count: 29`**, 26 `success` + 3 `skipped`, zero failures.

### The renderer was read first, and it decided the authoring shape

`aspect-ratio.tsx` reads `ratio`, `className`, `image` (with `alt`) and `children || body` — **never `content`**. The before-state was then measured by rendering each of the five through the real `SchemaRenderer`: **3 elements, empty text, zero images** for all five, i.e. the Radix ratio wrapper with nothing inside. 5 of 5 confirmed, and a repo-wide sweep for `type: 'aspect-ratio'` found no sixth site.

⭐ **The card's fix would not have been enough, and the developer caught why.** The four card demos needed `children` at **both** levels, because `ui:card` reads `title`/`description`/`header`/`children || body`/`footer` and **also never reads `content`** — moving only the outer key would have traded an empty ratio box for an **empty card**. That is the kind of thing only reading the second renderer finds.

### The gate verdict, reported either way as asked — and it is a "no" with four measured reasons

I asked whether anything would have caught this. The answer is **nothing would have**, and each reason is measured rather than argued:

1. `catalog-gallery-render.test.tsx` **does** render all five and passes — its `drewSomething` predicate is satisfied by the 3-element empty box, and its stronger authored-text control is scoped to a category this family is not in.
2. `BaseSchema` is `.passthrough()` with an index signature, so **zod and tsc both accept `content`** — these five are therefore not in #6318's `safeValidateSchema` population.
3. `check-doc-component-types.mjs` excludes the question **by name** in its own docblock.
4. The manifest tier reports `unknown-prop` — the same warning it gives a typo.

⭐ And the proposal is refused with its reason: a corpus-wide "container fixture must render its authored content" sweep is **not source-decidable**, because the predicate needs *"which authored key is this renderer's content slot"* — and `ui:aspect-ratio` declares `isContainer: true` while declaring **no `type:'slot'` input at all**, where `page:card` does declare one. ⇒ A sweep would have to guess the slot for the first shape. What **is** decidable is the per-family pin, and that is what shipped, at category scope rather than over five ids.

### Reverse verification without disk mutation

The pin's counter-probe renders the **exact pre-fix content shape** in-process and asserts empty text plus zero images, so the positive assertions cannot pass vacuously; a second counter-probe asserts the judge **does** see content authored under a read key. Direction observed matches the expectation.

### Two things declared rather than hidden

- ⚠️ One file sits just outside a literal reading of the fence — the per-issue pin beside the fixtures it pins, matching the shape a prior card of this same class used. Declared in the report as "one file to drop if PM disagrees". **I do not disagree**: a pin belongs with what it pins, and the alternative is a pin nobody finds.
- The four card demos also gained centering classes so the card fills the box, named as the one presentational addition. Fine, and named is the point.

### Filed from this work

**#6788** — `basic-context-menu` authors its trigger as a card with `content`, which `ui:card` never reads; measured 3 elements and empty text, the label surviving only as a leaked `content="…"` attribute. Same class, different family, and the **5th and last** card+`content` node in the catalog.

**Claim: `domain:ui` execution seat · PM session `session_01CRJge11jso9TpXRWFt1Z49` · round R13 · branch `claude/issue-6773-aspect-ratio-demos`**

⚠️ **Posted late — this marker was missing while the round ran.** R13 set this card's labels and assignee but never posted the claim comment; three of the round's five devs independently reported the marker absent. Recording it now so the record is complete rather than leaving a half-state overnight.

**Why this is not merely tidiness.** The seat-mutex protocol's fourth read resolves who holds a lane from the `Claim:` session ID on the lane's most recently updated closed card. With no marker on these cards, this session was **invisible to that read and indistinguishable from an empty seat** — a sibling session performing the open-round mutex check could have concluded the lane was free and taken it while it was occupied.

**Cause, recorded rather than excused.** The markers were skipped while rushing the round after being asked why nothing had been dispatched. Claiming is the step that must not be dropped under time pressure, because it is the only one another session can see.

Outcome: PR #6786, merged.
